sentences: The Fed held, Microsoft beat, Alphabet got crushed, and Bitcoin couldn’t hold above $81,000.
Here’s why that’s not a good sign for the bulls.
If you’ve been following along, you know I post here every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
This one is a day late on purpose.
Wednesday was packed with catalysts, and I trade off momentum, so I wasn’t going to write about where the market was heading before I saw which direction it actually picked.

Plenty of catalysts, and none of them were enough to push Bitcoin higher.
(Bitcoin chart showing the rejection above $81,000 after the Fed and earnings)
Bitcoin pushed above $81,000 after the Fed announcement and got rejected near $81,700.
Then it dumped back under $80,000 when Alphabet’s earnings hit.
As I write this, it’s sitting around $79,850, holding right below a level that used to be strong support.
When a level holds as support for weeks, breaks, and then price can’t get back above it, that old support becomes resistance.
Bitcoin had two shots at real momentum this week, the Fed and big tech earnings, and couldn’t use either one to reclaim it.
This is not a good sign for the bulls.
Go long strength, short weakness.
Right now Bitcoin is showing weakness.
Until it reclaims $80,000 and holds it, I’m not interested in longs.
If it gets rejected under $80,000 again, the $79,100 low from last weekend is the next level I’m watching.
If that breaks, the first dump probably isn’t the last dump… $75k is on the table.
If Bitcoin surprises and reclaims $81,000 with real momentum, I’ll change my mind.
That’s the whole point of trading off momentum instead of opinions.
